Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Obtain the PPR advertisement-period rule before publishing a day-count breach. The dates themselves are the portal's own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] Only 1 of 1,158 tenders is JICA-funded, so JICA does not govern these contracts. Use it as the international standard the package would have had to meet, never as 'JICA violation'. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [3] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [4] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [3] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [4] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The paragraph bites only on INTERNATIONAL competitive procurement and this dataset contains none — so the flag fires on a condition Para 4.4 never reaches. Report the inversion instead: running these as NCT is what keeps Para 4.4, Para 5.50 and Para 6.14 ('open international competitive procurement is the preferred approach for contracts of both high and substantial risk') out of reach. Feb 2025 also postdates most of these contracts. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). This information shall be kept posted … for at least thirty (30) days. / Format e-PG3A-C Note 1: For any agreement above BDT 10.00 Lac, Information on Beneficial Ownership need to be provided. || [5] 67.2 Within the timeline mentioned in the TDS from the issuance of the NOA but not later than the date specified therein … shall sign the contract. / TDS: within [mention number of days as per Rule 123(9) of the PPR 2025: 14/21/28] days … fourteen (14) days, where the estimated cost does not exceed BDT 50 million; twenty-one (21) days … BDT 50-250 million; twenty-eight (28) days, where the estimated cost exceeds BDT 250 million. / 67.3 Failure … to sign the Contract … shall constitute sufficient grounds for the annulment of the award and forfeiture of the Tender Security. || [6] 63.2 Within fourteen (14) days from the date of receipt of the NOA, the successful Tenderer shall furnish the Performance Security for the due performance of the Contract in the amount as stated under ITT Sub Clauses 62.1 or 62.2.
Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] The paragraph bites only on INTERNATIONAL competitive procurement and this dataset contains none — so the flag fires on a condition Para 4.4 never reaches. Report the inversion instead: running these as NCT is what keeps Para 4.4, Para 5.50 and Para 6.14 ('open international competitive procurement is the preferred approach for contracts of both high and substantial risk') out of reach. Feb 2025 also postdates most of these contracts. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] The paragraph bites only on INTERNATIONAL competitive procurement and this dataset contains none — so the flag fires on a condition Para 4.4 never reaches. Report the inversion instead: running these as NCT is what keeps Para 4.4, Para 5.50 and Para 6.14 ('open international competitive procurement is the preferred approach for contracts of both high and substantial risk') out of reach. Feb 2025 also postdates most of these contracts. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The paragraph bites only on INTERNATIONAL competitive procurement and this dataset contains none — so the flag fires on a condition Para 4.4 never reaches. Report the inversion instead: running these as NCT is what keeps Para 4.4, Para 5.50 and Para 6.14 ('open international competitive procurement is the preferred approach for contracts of both high and substantial risk') out of reach. Feb 2025 also postdates most of these contracts. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [4] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] The collection was scraped at a point in time; a notice may have been published after the scrape, or the status may be stale. Re-check the tender ID on eprocure.gov.bd before publishing.

So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Two separate over-reaches in the flag's own name. First, 5.01 governs INTERNATIONAL bidding and every tender here is national (NCT), so the 45 days never applied. Second, only 1 tender is JICA-funded. Drop the word 'Violation'; the usable form is that no window here would have satisfied an ICB timetable. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.
