Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Context for the under-14-day cases, not a finding of its own. || [3] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [4] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [5] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [6] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [7] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [8] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [2] The 80-100%-of-estimate band is the real test, and it cannot be run: Estimated_Cost is blank in all 1,158 records. So the honest claim is 'not testable', and this flag interlocks with the missing-estimate finding rather than standing alone. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [5] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [6] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [7] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Counter_Argument: [1] ITT 44.4 'There shall be no requirement as to the minimum number of responsive Tenders'; ITT 56.3 tenders may not be rejected if the lowest evaluated price conforms to market price. 56.2 is permissive ('can be'), so the question is whether the TEC considered it and what the HOPE decided — not that a rule was automatically broken. || [2] Highest-volume flag in the dataset (1,144 of 1,158). Publish as a documented pattern in the portal's own dates, not as a rule breach, until the governing PPR rule is obtained. || [3] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [4] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.

Counter_Argument: [1] A blank field on a printed page can be a portal rendering fault rather than an unpublished date. Re-pull the notice from eprocure.gov.bd before writing that a date was withheld. || [2] ITT 44.5: 'There shall be no automatic exclusion of Tenders which are above or below the official estimate.' So the finding is that the most direct test of price manipulation cannot be run — write 'impossible to verify', never 'violated'. || [3] Note 5 excuses State-Owned Enterprises, so check whether a winner is state-owned before naming it. The duty is split and that is the strength of this finding: 5.14 puts disclosure on the bidder, 68.1 puts publication on the procuring entity — neither can blame the e-GP software, and the 39 notices that do carry the table are the proof: the field works when someone fills it in. || [4] The 28 days is NOT in ITT 67.2 — it is one of three TDS bands, and only 24 of 645 awards clear BDT 25 cr. Also: the band keys off the ESTIMATED cost, which is blank everywhere, so contract value is used as a stand-in here and the band may be wrong in either direction. Always cite 'ITT 67.2 read with PPR 2025 Rule 123(9)'. || [5] The field is blank in the REGISTER; many award PDFs do print a yes/no. Where the PDF answers, that answer is used instead and this flag is not raised. Treat a remaining blank as an unanswerable question, not as a missed deadline.
